title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of accessibility testing methods, tools, and auditing.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of accessibility issues can automated tools detect?
questions.explanation: Automated tools catch only about 20‑30% of issues; manual and user testing are essential.

questions.question: Which browser extension is considered the industry standard for automated accessibility testing?
questions.explanation: axe DevTools, powered by axe‑core, is the most widely used engine and is integrated into many other tools.

questions.question: A Lighthouse accessibility score of 100 means the website is fully accessible.
questions.explanation: A perfect Lighthouse score only means no automated issues were found; manual testing is still required.

questions.question: Which of the following is a manual accessibility test?
options: Navigating a page using only the Tab key
questions.explanation: Keyboard navigation requires a human to judge focus order and visibility.

questions.question: To test reflow, zoom the browser to _____ % and ensure no horizontal scrolling is required.
questions.explanation: WCAG 1.4.4 requires content to work at 200% zoom.

questions.question: What is the VoiceOver modifier key (VO) by default on macOS?
questions.explanation: Control+Option is the default VoiceOver modifier.

questions.question: Screen readers rely on CSS to understand the page structure.
questions.explanation: Screen readers use the accessibility tree, built from the DOM and ARIA, not visual CSS.

questions.question: Which NVDA shortcut opens the Elements List (links, headings, landmarks)?
questions.explanation: NVDA + F7 displays a list of links, headings, and landmarks.

questions.question: When auditing a website, why is it important to select a representative sample of pages?
options: Because different templates and components may have different issues
To test only the home page
questions.explanation: Issues often reside in specific page types (forms, modals, etc.) that aren't on the home page.

questions.question: An audit finding states a button has no accessible name. Which WCAG criterion is most directly violated?
questions.explanation: 4.1.2 requires interactive elements to have a programmatically determined name.

questions.question: Automated tools like axe can determine if the focus order of a page is logical.
questions.explanation: Focus order requires human judgment; axe can only detect if elements are focusable, not if the order makes sense.

questions.question: What does 'shift left' mean in the context of accessibility?
options: Move testing earlier in the development cycle
questions.explanation: Shift left means integrating testing into design, development, and CI to catch issues early.

questions.question: Which npm package can you use to run axe in a Playwright test?
questions.explanation: `@axe-core/playwright` integrates axe into Playwright tests.

questions.question: What is the purpose of failing a build when an accessibility violation is found?
options: To prevent new accessibility bugs from reaching production
questions.explanation: Build failures block merging until issues are fixed, preventing regressions.

questions.question: It's acceptable to rely solely on automated accessibility testing if you run it on every commit.
questions.explanation: Automated tools miss many issues; manual and user testing are always required.

questions.question: What is the best way to test colour contrast?
options: Use a contrast checker tool (WebAIM, axe)
questions.explanation: Contrast checkers measure the exact ratio between foreground and background colors.

questions.question: Why is it important to test with a screen reader even if your automated tools pass?
options: Because automated tools can't hear the page
To verify the actual user experience and announcements
questions.explanation: Only a screen reader reveals what is actually announced to users, including missing context or confusing sequences.

questions.question: Which tool provides a visual overlay of headings, landmarks, and ARIA on a page?
questions.explanation: WAVE overlays icons directly on the page for visual inspection.

questions.question: In an audit report, what does 'impact' typically refer to?
options: The severity of the accessibility barrier
questions.explanation: Impact indicates how severely the issue affects users (critical, serious, moderate, minor).

questions.question: Only the QA team needs to learn about accessibility testing.
questions.explanation: Accessibility is a shared responsibility across design, development, testing, and product management.

questions.question: When should accessibility testing be performed in a project?
options: At the very end before launch
Continuously throughout design, development, and after deployment
Never, if automated tools are used
questions.explanation: Testing early and often reduces cost and ensures better outcomes.

questions.question: Which WCAG criterion requires that content can be operated through a keyboard interface?
questions.explanation: 2.1.1 mandates keyboard operability.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of integrating axe into a CI/CD pipeline?
options: It catches accessibility regressions automatically on each code change
questions.explanation: Automated checks in CI prevent new violations from being merged.

questions.question: How can you test if information is not conveyed by colour alone?
options: View the page in greyscale (e.g., Achromatopsia emulation in DevTools)
questions.explanation: Greyscale shows whether meaning is lost without colour.
